video.title: The Magic of Single-Foot Forehand Training

classification.reason: The coach uses video demonstrations of himself and a high-level demonstrator to teach forehand probing footwork and loading mechanics using a single-foot drill.

problem.title_as_question: Why do players struggle with forehand weight transfer and foot positioning, and how does single-foot training improve probing?
problem.definition: Players fail to move deep enough into the forehand corner to set their rear loading foot behind the ball, preventing body weight transfer through the shot and forcing an arm-dominated reaching swing.
prerequisites: open or semi-open stance loading mechanics

symptoms.description: The player exhibits no forward weight transfer through the shot during the forward swing.
The player reaches with the arm and curls the racket around the ball rather than driving forward.
Contact with the ball never feels clean, comfortable, or solid to the player.
The upper body leans and adjusts awkwardly on almost every shot to compensate for spacing errors.

causes.statement: The rear loading foot fails to get behind the ball and cannot press through the court into the shot.
The player does not run deep enough into the forehand corner to set up their base behind the ball.

angles.summary: Shot power and natural body unloading require the loading foot to be placed behind the ball so body weight can press through the court toward the target.
Contrasting the demonstrator's clean probing and repeatable swing with the coach's uneven tracking and constant upper-body compensations.
Debunking the idea that a player should take an identical rigid swing on every shot regardless of positioning, instead of adapting to the ball seen.
Reaching with the arm to curl the ball around may occasionally make the court, but it will never feel solid or clean.
Visualizing the loading foot reaching deep into the corner and pressing back out into the court along the line of the shot.

solutions.summary: Practice probing and hitting forehands while balanced entirely on one foot to heavily punish poor positioning and build heightened visual and physical tracking.
solutions.external_goal: Probe on one foot and hit incoming tossed balls cleanly through the court.

solutions.summary: Look at the ball and swing through the ball that you actually see in front of you rather than executing a pre-planned rigid swing.
solutions.external_goal: Look at the ball and swing through the ball that is seen.

solutions.summary: Use your body to dynamically adjust and lean into the ball so that your racket path through the contact zone remains consistent despite imperfect probing.
On wide balls, reach the loading foot out behind the ball and actively press it back toward the court through the shot.
solutions.external_goal: Press the loading foot back towards the court.
